limits: The change reuses caller-owned FFT scratch instead of RustFFT process() allocating scratch per transform. It preserves FFT, sparse kernels, smoothing, feature arithmetic, body ownership, policy, routing and evaluation-time defaults.

Each streaming analyzer now retains get_inplace_scratch_len() Complex32 values allocated at construction; cloning copies this buffer. This trades persistent bounded memory for removing repeated allocation. Whole-system memory acceptance is not established.

Audio and semantic comparisons canonicalize record order and remove timing. Both buses have756 common observations per comparison. The allocation regression proves the measured NSGT call path, not all allocations in body extraction or runtime.

Resource measurements are whole-run wall time, not thread CPU time. Histogram p99 is a bounded nearest-rank interval. Offline whole-hop timing includes deterministic body completion waits. Keep every paired timing result; allocation removal alone does not establish a speedup or resource acceptance.

Six-second hold/flow runs are not full-duration, full-eight-prototype or live-device acceptance. Physical prototype transfer validity, non-energy consequences, full conditional default and remaining normal integrations are incomplete. I10 incomplete; I9 held; I11 disabled.
